## Proposed Schedule Management Plan

### Purpose And Scope

The schedule control method covers approved work packages, activities, milestones, dependencies, gates, evidence readiness, forecast updates, fallback triggers, and baseline decisions for the Option B application delivery. The approved backlog contains nine work packages and the delivery plan contains the proposed phase and gate sequence. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-backlog.md`, lines 19-31 and 75-83; `projects/lead-lab/artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 84-151]

| Level | Schedule content | Control rule |

| Outcome | Option B application available before the 2026-09-11 program start, or SharePoint fallback remains available | Preserve the fixed program constraint and fallback path. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/CONTEXT.md`, lines 4 and 19; `projects/lead-lab/artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 202-214] |

Leave duration and owner TBD when not evidenced. | Milestone | Gate 1, Gate 2, feature complete/freeze, go/no-go, production readiness, final approval, launch, and program start | Track date or window, entry condition, evidence state, dependencies, decision authority, forecast state, and fallback result. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/artifacts/lead-lab-web-app-delivery-plan.md`, lines 84-151; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/03-perform-process/draft-output.md`, lines 20-31] |

### Planning Method

1. Use rolling-wave planning. Detail the next gate and the work needed to make its evidence decision-ready.
2. Use milestone and gate tracking for later work until activity durations, resource calendars, and dependencies are evidenced.
3. Do not infer duration, float, or resource loading from the recorded capacity range. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/application/environment/gate-1-environment-and-ownership.md`, lines 20-24 and 79-83; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, lines 18-22]
4. Refresh the detailed forecast after the 2026-08-25 Gate 1 reassessment and before the 2026-09-04 go/no-go review. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/registers/decision-log.md`, D-22; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 17-19]

### Tolerance And Escalation

Numeric schedule tolerances are not configured. The smallest useful provisional rule is to require PM review when any of the following occurs:

- The go/no-go or launch target moves.
- A gate fails or cannot be evidenced by its review point.
- A critical-path dependency remains unresolved at its needed-by point.
- Production preparation cannot finish before the proposed launch date.
- A forecast cannot be supported by confirmed owner, calendar, or activity evidence.

These are proposed review triggers, not approved tolerance thresholds. [Sources: `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/project-control.md`, lines 68-76; `projects/lead-lab/pm-control/runs/2026-08-21-pm-17-develop-schedule/stages/04-validate-and-review/review-record.md`, findings 1-7; `workspaces/alson-pm-control/references/authority-rules.md`, lines 23-30]

## Recommendation

Approve the formal rolling-wave schedule-management approach as a proposed control set, but do not approve a schedule baseline or committed launch date. Resolve the schedule carrier and owner, complete the Gate 1 reassessment on 2026-08-25, create the calendar only when its inputs are confirmed, and refresh PM-17 before the conditional 2026-09-04 go/no-go review.
